narrative_purpose: A triptych of senses humans entirely lack — a shark reading electric fields in water, a bat building a world from returning echoes, a fish feeling water flow along its lateral line — so the reader feels how many whole channels of reality exist beyond our own.
subject: Three small naturalist vignettes joined by darkness. Left: a shark gliding low over the seabed, faint electric-field haloes glowing around a hidden prey shape buried in sand. Middle: a bat in flight with concentric sound-echo rings rippling out to a moth ahead. Right: a fish with a glowing line of tiny sensor pits along its flank, swirls of disturbed water rendered as faint cyan eddies around it.
scene: Three dark vignettes — two underwater, one in night air — each in its own pool of cool glow against deep indigo, separated by shadow.
camera: Three balanced side-by-side naturalist studies, mid-distance on each animal.
light: Cool bioluminescent-style key picking each animal from the dark; the sensed field/echo/flow rendered as faint living glow; deep indigo surround.
palette: Void-indigo ground, Pandora cyan and living teal for the sensed phenomena and animal rims, a sparse magenta accent.
style: Painterly speculative-biology naturalist plate, hand-painted, observed.
detail_level: Crisp on each animal and its sensed phenomenon; backgrounds dissolving into haze.
composition: Three equal panels of dark negative space, each animal offset so the sensed field has room to glow.
consistency_notes: Earth animals but rendered in the same cool Pandora palette and from-within glow as the rest of the chapter, so they sit in one visual world.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no logos, no diagram labels, no arrows, no hard panel borders, no photographic or 3D-render look, no lens flares, no neon UI glow, no cartoon or anime style
